# Net.Agora.Android

.NET for Android / .NET MAUI bindings for Agora's native Android SDKs, generated by `class-parse`.
This is the only repository that binds them; [`sbokatuk/Net.Agora`](https://github.com/sbokatuk/Net.Agora)
(cross-platform façade) and [`sbokatuk/Net.Agora.iOS`](https://github.com/sbokatuk/Net.Agora.iOS)
consume what is published here and release on their own cadence. Seven products —
Video, Voice, Signaling, Chat, IoT, Whiteboard, Fastboard — plus twelve
`Net.Agora.Extensions.<Name>.Android` native-payload packages.

## Sources of truth — edit these, never a second copy

| File | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `Directory.Build.props` | Every native version pin and binding revision (`Agora<Product>Version` / `Agora<Product>BindingRevision`) |
| `build/pins.sh` | The *only* shell parser of those pins; source it (`. ./build/pins.sh`), never re-grep the props |
| `build/packages.tsv` | The package set. Adding a package = a row here + a project under `src/` |
| `build/tracks.tsv` | Release tracks and their git-tag prefixes |
| `build/upstream.tsv` | What the daily drift check watches |
| `build/checksums.txt` | SHA-256 of every native artifact, by `group:artifact:version` |

Package version is `<native SDK version>.<binding revision>`. Bump the revision when the binding or
packaging changes and the native pin does not. The products sit on unrelated native lines (RTC
4.6.x, RTM 2.2.x, Chat 1.4.x, IoT 1.3.x, Whiteboard 2.16.x, Fastboard 1.8.x), so never stamp one
version across the set, and never "align" the Android pins with `Net.Agora.iOS` — Android running
ahead is legitimate.

When a native pin moves, in the same change: refresh `build/checksums.txt` with
`./build/verify-artifacts.sh --print` (check *why* a hash changed before recording it), update the
size floors in `tests/Net.Agora.Android.PackageTests/Packages.cs` if the artifact's shape changed,
and add `docs/release-notes/<tag>.md`.

## Commands

```sh
dotnet build Net.Agora.Android.sln                      # no MAUI workload needed: samples are not in the sln
dotnet build src/Net.Agora.Video.Android/Net.Agora.Video.Android.csproj -f net9.0-android35.0
./build/BuildNugets.sh [--track rtc] [--suffix beta.12.34]   # packs into ./artifacts
dotnet test tests/Net.Agora.Android.PackageTests        # runs against the packed .nupkg, so pack first
./build/verify-artifacts.sh                             # bytes vs build/checksums.txt
. ./build/pins.sh && ./.github/scripts/run-emulator-tests.sh "$AGORA_VIDEO_PACKAGE_VERSION" net9.0-android35.0 Video
```

Nothing is fetched or vendored by hand: the `.aar` comes from Maven Central (or JitPack for the
netless products) at build time. Never commit an `.aar`, a `.nupkg` or anything else to `artifacts/`.

## Target frameworks and the two-pass pack

`AgoraSdkBand=net9` → `net8.0-android34.0;net9.0-android35.0`; `AgoraSdkBand=net10` →
`net10.0-android36.0`. API levels are pinned deliberately — they become the `lib/<tfm>/` folder
name, so never drop back to a bare `net8.0-android`. No single SDK covers all three, so
`build/BuildNugets.sh` packs twice (the second pass from a scratch `global.json`) and merges with
`build/merge-packages.py`. Keep those pass directories outside `artifacts/`.

`AndroidMavenLibrary` does not exist on `net8.0-android34.0`, and MSBuild ignores unknown items
silently: the build "succeeds" with an empty few-KB binding assembly. `src/Agora.Binding.props`
covers that with a `DownloadFile` target, and the package tests exist to catch it. Treat any change
to artifact resolution as needing proof on all three target frameworks.

## Working in this repository

- Add a package: row in `build/packages.tsv` (dependency order), project under
  `src/Net.Agora.<Id>.Android/`, coordinates in `build/checksums.txt`, a row in
  `build/upstream.tsv` if it tracks a new native SDK, a track in `build/tracks.tsv` if it releases
  on its own tag, and entries in `tests/Net.Agora.Android.PackageTests/Packages.cs`.
- Keep the existing comments and write in their style: explain *why*, name the failure mode the
  code prevents, and cite the file or artifact that proves it. Do not delete a rationale comment
  because the code around it moved.
- Do not add a `Directory.Build.props` under `src/`; the shared logic is imported explicitly by
  each `.csproj` (see `src/Agora.Binding.props` for the ordering reason).
- Every public hand-written member carries XML documentation. Generated members do not (CS1591 is
  suppressed permanently — Agora ships no javadoc to import).
- Prefer a Microsoft-published NuGet binding over embedding a third-party `.aar`: a second copy of
  `okio`, Kotlin or AndroidX fails a consuming app's dex merge.
- Video and Voice bind the same Java classes and are mutually exclusive in one app; IoT is
  exclusive with everything. Never introduce a reference that puts two of them together.

## Releases and CI

Merging `docs/release-notes/<tag>.md` to `main` *is* the release: `auto-release.yml` tags the merge
commit and dispatches `release.yml`. One tag releases one track — bare `v` for RTC (Video, Voice,
the twelve extensions), `signaling-v`, `chat-v`, `iot-v`, `whiteboard-v`, `fastboard-v`. Tag names
are four-part (`v4.6.3.5`, `chat-v1.4.0.2`).

`build.yml` is called by `pr.yml` and `release.yml`; pull requests run the full verification
(package tests, sample Release+R8 link, emulator legs) and publish `-beta.<pr>.<run>` packages,
while a release packs only its track and trusts the verification the merged commit already passed.
Keep `verify`/`track`/`suffix` semantics identical to the sibling repositories when touching CI.
